greet.title: Greeting and closing
greet.means: Open with Salam and the short name of the person the ticket is assigned to right now. Close with one of his five closings, picked by judgement. Nothing after it.
rules: First line: Salam <short name>, (Redmine) or Hi infra, (infra).
Greet the person who routed the question to us, not the original asker.
Closing, picked by judgement (miya 2026-10-27, #285768). Default: Thank you.
Thank you very much. = a large ticket: 3 or more fixes in the note, a PROD patch, a long review or rework, or a ticket that came back more than once.
Thank you <short name>. (or Thanks <short name>.) = the reader does extra for us: re-tests, re-routes, or is not the usual BA (QA, another team's developer).
Thanks. = a one-line developer hand-over (please find the fix at ...) or a quick alter note.
Terima kasih. = the note is written in Malay.

Out-of-the-norm closing (Thank you in abundance. / Thank you & Godspeed.) = ONLY when the other person started that tone first, e.g. a ticket by Ammar Zakwan. Never as an opener of my own (miya 2026-10-27).

His closings in 134 Redmine notes (May to Oct 2026): Thank you. 103 · Thanks 16 · Thank you very much 10 · with a name 3 · Terima kasih 2. Size alone does not decide: 17 large notes still end Thank you.

lean.title: Only what is needed
lean.means: Say only what the reader does not have yet. No lead-in sentence, no restating the ticket, no closing remarks, stop after the last item.
rules: No lead-in words: Everything starts from X -> Start from X.
Do not restate the ticket, the expected behaviour or the test data unless asked.
No verdict words about our own work (verified, DB-proven, as mentioned).

No pushback lines to another team (miya 2026-10-14, #282303): never say what we will not do, never compare their version or work against ours to refuse, never tell them to raise a ticket. State the finding only; they decide the next step.

Every draft reply to another person comes in 2 versions: SHORT first (1-2 lines, the answer only, e.g. "Bukan id ni je... Isu ni akan jadi untuk semua permohonan yang isi tanah dimiliki."), then FULL. He picks one.

A chat reply answers ONLY the question in the last message, in about 3 short fragments. No background on how it works today and no process line (change request, please confirm) unless that message asks for it (ADHOC-UPP-PDTJ: 5 lines cut to "Sepatutnya waktu dijana. Waktu ADO sign tu ke. Jana semula load balik tarikh ADO sign.").

line.title: Lines and sentences
line.means: Short sentences. A sentence that continues the one before it stays on the same line, up to 2 sentences. Then a new line. Never two facts joined into one sentence.
rules: At most 2 sentences on one line.
Related or continuing sentences share a line. A new point starts a new line.
A sentence joined by jadi / so / sebab / bila that carries two facts is split.
Never list 3 or more ids or items inside one sentence. Use a list or summarise.
banned: 3 or more sentences on one line
a long sentence joined by jadi / so

table.title: Tables for data
table.means: Field, table and column data goes in a table. On Redmine that is a Textile table.
rules: Field / Table / Column answers are a table, one row per field.
Redmine tables: |_. Head |_. Head | then | cell | cell |.
Column and table names inside a sentence go in @...@ on Redmine.
banned: Table : / Column : label lines when a table fits

separate.title: One kind of thing per section
separate.means: Each kind of content has its own section: the explanation, the mapping tables, the scripts. Never a script inside the mapping, never a note inside the script.
rules: Order: opener, short explanation, tables, then Scripts as its own section.
A script block never sits between two mapping tables.
banned: a SQL block before the last mapping table

script.title: Scripts for another developer
script.means: A script shows exactly the columns the reader asked about, one clause per line, and can be pasted into any schema.
rules: One clause per line: SELECT / FROM / WHERE / AND / ORDER BY.
Select the mapped columns only, not SELECT *.
No JOIN. Resolve ids with a subquery.
No schema prefix.
banned: a whole script on one line

proven.title: Every rule sentence is counted first
proven.means: A sentence that states how the system behaves is written only after it was counted or read this session. What was not checked is said as not checked, to miya, never inside the note.
rules: Before a rule sentence: which query or code line backs it, and across how many rows.
One sample is not a rule. Count the table.
Check the code and a second environment before calling it true or test data.
Self-audit before the hand-back: read the note as the reader. A frequency word must match the count (11 of 36 is not sometimes). A cause is named, never called a factor.
banned: a rule sentence backed by one row
sometimes / rarely / kadang-kadang where a count exists
uncontrolled factors / certain cases with the factor not named
proven.ask: For each sentence that states system behaviour: name the query or code line and the count behind it. Then the self-audit: does every how-often word match that count, and is every cause named in words the reader knows?

plain.title: Plain words for BA
plain.means: A BA reads it. No file names, line numbers, class names or code words. Say what the user now sees.
rules: No file:line, no .java / .xhtml names, no method names.
No capital letters for emphasis.
One fix per line, in the words of the screen.

rojak.title: His everyday mixed language
rojak.means: When the note is in Malay it is his rojak, not formal Malay. Developer words stay English. Connectors are casual English.
rules: tak / dah / amik / je, not tidak dapat / dihantar / dipaparkan.
Refer, commit, merge, branch, table, value stay English.
Basically / Actually / so / just, not Ringkasnya / Oleh itu.
A thinking pause is written "..." (Kalau nak test kat staging... P_APLIKASI_ID 62405). A line that sums up opens with "So untuk <x>:". A table-to-table path is written with "-->".

hint.title: Hints for a junior
hint.means: A junior gets where to look and what to compare. Never the cause, the script or the diff.
rules: Each item: symptom, where to start, test data.
No sentence that says why it breaks.
hint.ask: Does any line say why it breaks or give the finished fix? Cut it.

topdown.title: Top-down explanation
topdown.means: Explain from the highest view down. First the issue as the user sees it and where. Then one layer at a time, each cause in its own block, going down. Then where it is fixed. Last, what the reader checks to see it work.
rules: Line after the greeting: the issue at the top view (screen, action, env, which urusan or module).
Two or more causes: say how many, then one numbered block per cause, each opening with what the user sees for that cause.
Inside a block, go down one layer per line: screen or action, then the data or flow, then the code. Class names and line numbers only on the lowest layer.
The fix comes after its cause, never before the issue is said.
Close with what the reader checks: the permohonan, the screen, the click.
(miya 2026-10-30, #239386: explain top-down, from the issue at the top view, layer by layer to where we fix, and for them to check.)
banned: a class name, line number or fix in the first line after the greeting
a hand-over with no line saying what the reader checks
topdown.ask: Read only the line after the greeting: does it say what the user sees and where, with no class name or line number? Does each cause go down one layer per line and close on the fix? Is the last line before the closing what the reader checks?
